learning_outcomes.text: Ability to apply the knowledge of the theory of elasticity and plasticity to solve problems of structural integrity assessment of materials, components and structures.
Ability to apply theoretical models and to use physical and mathematical tools for problem diagnosis and resolution.
Know the contents developed in the module.
Know the theoretical bases of elasticity and plasticity, and the bases for their application to the evaluation and design of components.
Deeply understand the elasto-plastic behavior of structural materials.
Analyze complex structures and components working in elasto-plastic regime.
Write a scientific paper concisely and present it clearly.

syllabus_topics: Stresses: Stress state (at point, in plane, three-dimensional). Changes in reference system. Principal stresses and directions. Mohr's circle for stresses. Plane stress state.

Deformations: Deformation state (three-dimensional). Theory of finite deformations. Theory of small deformations. Principal deformations and directions. Mohr's circle for deformations. Plane deformation state.

Elasticity: Isotropic linear elasticity. Constitutive equations. Hooke's Law. Lamé's equations. Strain energy. Poisson's ratio limits. Anisotropic linear elasticity. Constitutive equations for anisotropic materials. Orthotropic material. Transversely isotropic material. Linear thermoelasticity. Applications of constitutive equations for anisotropic materials.

Plasticity: Mechanisms of plastic deformation. The tensile test. Empirical laws for stress-strain equations. Yield criteria for isotropic materials (Tresca, Von Mises, Mohr-Coulomb, Drucker-Prager, etc.). Yield criteria for anisotropic materials (Hill, Tsai-Hill). Isotropic and kinematic hardening. Constitutive equations of plasticity (Prandtl-Reuss). Applications in plastic regime.
assessment_rules: The final grade for the ordinary call is calculated as 0.6 EF + 0.4 PEC. No minimum grade is required in the final exam or continuous assessment tests. The extraordinary call consists of a written exam (EF) where the contents of the subject will be evaluated, and the final grade is also calculated as 0.6 EF + 0.4 PEC.
